body.p: In the Office Action, claims 1-9, 12-14 and 16-17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. Amended claim 1 recites, among other things a "fastening system configured to attach a fixture to a monument provided for installation in a passenger cabin," and does not positively recite the monument within the body of claim 1. Additionally, claims 16 and 17 have been amended to depend from claim 14, and the intended scope of claim 1 is clear for the purposes of Section 112. Accordingly, Applicant respectfully traverses the Section 112 rejection.

Additionally, claims 1-6 and 12-17 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by Seeley et al. (US 6,561,600). Claims 7-9 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Chavarria et al. (US 11,365,006). Applicant respectfully traverses the foregoing and requests reconsideration.

Notwithstanding the foregoing traversal, solely in an effort to expedite prosecution, Applicant had amended claim 1 to recite "the frame is moved relative to the wall portion in a fastening direction which extends vertically downward until the at least two first fastening elements engage respective ones of the at least two second fastening elements, wherein each of the at least two first fastening elements are displaced from one another along the fastening direction, and wherein each of the at least two second fastening elements are displaced from one another along the fastening direction." This amendment is fully supported and adds no new matter. See Published Application FIGs. 3-4; 0053- 57. Claim 15 has been similarly amended.

Applicant's FIGs. 3-4 show the fastening system 18 in a pre-assembled state and in a fastened state, respectively. "Starting from the pre-assembled state, the frame 20 is moved in a fastening direction 54 which extends parallel to the main extension direction 44." Published Application 0056. As shown in the annotated version of Applicant's FIG. 3, the fastening direction 54 extends vertically downward, each the at least two first

fastening elements 24 are displaced from one another along the fastening direction 54 and each of the at least two fastening elements 26 are displaced from one another along the fastening direction 54.
lines 61-64; see also Seeley Col. 2, lines 52-54 ("The cam latch is created and engaged via the rotational assembly of the respective panels.").

Therefore, Seeley discloses a plurality of extensions 225 and 240 which are horizontally aligned in a direction perpendicular to a fastening direction of the front and back panels 210, 215. Moreover, modifying Seeley according to claims 1 and 15 would render Seeley inoperable. Chavarria fails to resolve the deficiencies of Seeley.

Accordingly, even if combined, a point Applicant does not concede, the resulting combination of the cited references fails to disclose or suggest all of the features of claim 1. Thus, claim 1 should be allowable over the cited art. Those claims that depend therefrom should be allowable as well-at least by virtue of their claim dependency.

Finally, Applicant has added new claims 18-20 which are fully supported and add no new matter. See claim 1; see also Published Application FIGs. 3-4; 0053-60. Applicant respectfully submits that claims 18-20 are allowable over the cited references.

Applicant therefore respectfully submits that all of the claims of the application should be found to be allowable and thus requests that the Examiner indicate all of the claims as allowed and pass the application to allowance.

Furthermore, the fact that Applicant has only addressed certain rejections should not be considered to be acquiescence to the rejections. Rather, Applicant has presented the argument herein in an effort to expedite prosecution. Applicant reserves any and all rights to address any rejection made but not specifically addressed herein.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees which may be required to this application under 37 C.F.R. §§ 1.16-1.17, or credit any overpayment, to Deposit Account No. 07-2069.
Should the Examiner discover there are remaining issues which may be resolved by a telephone interview, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned attorney at (312) 600-6841.
